summary:
Research product recording a new high-consequence Surface on the accepted map (base version 10), preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

New sourced lead, prompted by the log/snapshot position mechanism recorded last turn: the snapshot receive path updates lastApplied and lastSnapshot but never calls setLastLog — the only setLastLog callers are NewRaft, liveBootstrap, restoreUserSnapshot, dispatchLogs and appendEntries (raft.go:1928-1953). Its compaction also removes entries only up to the installed snapshot index (snapshot.go:213-259, maxLog = min(snapIdx, lastLogIdx-trailing)), so a follower that already holds a longer divergent branch keeps that tail. getLastEntry therefore continues to report the tail's index/term during the window, even though the FSM state and the committed/latest configuration now come from the installed snapshot.

Deliberately recorded as a Surface rather than escalated: both premises are unresolved. Reachability requires a follower whose log is longer than the installed snapshot (the leader sends a snapshot when its own log no longer covers the follower's nextIndex, and a longer divergent branch can drive that state, but the exact sequence was not established). The consequence is also unmeasured — vote comparisons use getLastEntry, so the follower's self-report and vote decisions reflect the tail until the next matching AppendEntries truncates it and calls setLastLog. No behavior, fact, requirement or previously accepted Surface disposition was changed, so the three confirmed findings and every accepted result keep their original basis.

Also preserved: the ReloadConfig notification-scope lead, and the open reachability/consequence premises behind the three confirmed violations (batching-FSM ConfigurationStore delivery, heartbeat fast-path header gate, TimeoutNow sender attribution).
